winged adjective

also feathered, with wings

classical

Plin. NH 11.1: apēs (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Met. 7.350: serpentēs (Lewis & Short)

pennātus, pennāta, pennātum

declension

feathered, winged

From penna; also written pinnātus.

Other words

  • ālātus, ālāta, ālātum — having wings

    declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 4.259: plantae (Lewis & Short); Ov. F. 5.666: pēs (Lewis & Short)

    (poetic)

    From āla.

Examples

  • intereā pavidam volitāns pennāta per urbem nūntia Fāma ruit

    meanwhile winged Rumour rushes with the news, flitting through the frightened cityVerg. A. 9.473–474

See also wing, feather, bird, fly, flutter, wing.
